channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: Reusse: Unbeaten Bethel’s strong defense powered by defensive back Devin Williams
item.description: The Royals play host to Wisconsin-Platteville on Saturday in the NCAA Division III playoffs.

item.title: Frank Gehry, the most celebrated architect of his time, dies at 96
item.description: Frank Gehry, who designed some of the most imaginative buildings ever constructed and achieved a level of worldwide acclaim seldom afforded any architect, has died. He was 96.

item.title: Twins intend to keep Joe Ryan, Pablo López and Byron Buxton, despite trade rumors
item.description: The Twins don’t plan to tear their roster down further, increasing the likelihood that their top players will remain on the team in 2026.

item.title: For $2.25M, a concrete compound in Farmington ‘ideal for doomsday preppers’
item.description: A former Cold War-era missile launch site is among three Minnesota listings with their own “safe rooms.”

item.title: ICE announces a dozen Minneapolis arrests in ‘Operation Metro Surge’
item.description: The men arrested are from Mexico, Somalia and El Salvador.

item.title: Rosemount police chief blasts city process that led to his resignation after two months on leave
item.description: The Rosemount City Council approved a roughly $164,000 separation agreement following anonymous employee survey complaints.

item.title: Wells for drinking water near possible Minnesota mine tainted with manganese
item.description: A citizens group is testing wells as North Star Manganese tries to develop a mine. More than half the sites tested high enough that the water cannot be used in infant formula.

item.title: Fair State Brewing announces it will close after this weekend
item.description: The Minneapolis brewery told its members it was no longer a “fully functional business.”

item.title: Minneapolis Police Department blows budget by $19.6 million; council leaders call it ‘mismanagement’
item.description: Police Chief Brian O’Hara says it’s costly to replenish the ranks because new hires need training while existing officers rack up OT.

item.title: What we know about the Lutsen Resort arson case and the owner charged with setting the fire
item.description: Bryce Campbell, of Canada, bought the resort in 2018. It burned to the ground in 2024.
